stem: What is a distinguishing clinical feature of a night terror compared to a nightmare?

options.text: The child has no recall of the event in the morning
The child is easily consoled by a caregiver during the episode
The episode typically occurs during REM sleep in the last third of the night
The child can describe the 'bad dream' in vivid detail

explanation: Night terrors occur during non-REM sleep and are characterized by a complete lack of memory of the episode upon waking.
rationale: Focus on the child's memory and state of consciousness during and after the event.

optionExplanations.A: Night terrors occur during non-REM sleep and are characterized by a complete lack of memory of the episode upon waking.
optionExplanations.B: Children experiencing night terrors are typically inconsolable and may not even recognize their parents, unlike those having nightmares.
optionExplanations.C: This description fits nightmares; night terrors occur during non-REM sleep, usually in the first third of the night.
optionExplanations.D: Vivid recall is a hallmark of nightmares, whereas night terrors leave the child with no memory of the event.

source.hint: Focus on the child's memory and state of consciousness during and after the event.
